blocks.text: Have you ever wondered why the moon stays in orbit around the Earth or why objects fall to the ground? The answer lies in the fascinating concept of gravitation.

blocks.markdown: Gravitation is a fundamental force of nature that attracts two bodies towards each other. This force is responsible for keeping planets in orbit around the sun and for objects falling to the ground on Earth.

blocks.title: Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation
blocks.text: Newton's law states that every particle of matter in the universe attracts every other particle with a force that is directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centers.

blocks.markdown: Mathematically, Newton's law of gravitation is expressed as: $F = \frac{Gm_1m_2}{r^2}$, where $F$ is the gravitational force, $G$ is the gravitational constant, $m_1$ and $m_2$ are the masses, and $r$ is the distance between the centers of the two masses.

blocks.title: Calculating Gravitational Force
blocks.prompt: Calculate the gravitational force between two masses of 5 kg and 10 kg separated by a distance of 2 meters. Use $G = 6.674 \times 10^{-11} \text{Nm}^2/\text{kg}^2$.

steps.text: Identify the given values: $m_1 = 5 \text{ kg}$, $m_2 = 10 \text{ kg}$, $r = 2 \text{ m}$, and $G = 6.674 \times 10^{-11} \text{Nm}^2/\text{kg}^2$.

blocks.markdown: The gravitational force also explains the acceleration due to gravity, $g$, on the surface of the Earth. This is related to the mass and radius of the Earth.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Remember, the value of $g$ on Earth's surface is approximately $9.8 \text{ m/s}^2$. This is derived from $g = \frac{GM}{R^2}$, where $M$ is Earth's mass and $R$ is its radius.

blocks.markdown: Satellites stay in orbit due to the balance between gravitational force and their tangential velocity. They are constantly falling towards Earth but have enough horizontal speed to keep missing it, thus staying in orbit.

points: Newton's law of gravitation explains the force between two masses.
The gravitational force is crucial for understanding orbital motion and the value of $g$ on Earth.
